paper.title: Beyond Binary: Continuous State Optimization with Graph-Structured Objectives

settings.name_in_paper: Graph-structured linear bandit with movement costs (continuous state space)
unmapped: State s in [0,1]^k; loss is sum over k criteria of <phi_i(s|_{N(i)}), theta_i*> where phi_i depends only on the neighborhood N(i) in a known dependency graph
Learner observes the vector of k per-criterion noisy losses (not only the scalar total)
Movement cost lambda*||s_t - s_{t-1}||_1 added to regret (magnitude-based switching cost)
The learner knows the dependency graph G and the feature maps phi_i

Movement cost lambda*||s_t - s_{t-1}||_1 added to regret
The learner knows the dependency graph

settings.name_in_paper: Graph-structured linear bandit with movement costs, unknown dependency graph
unmapped: Dependency graph unknown; true parameters supported on true neighborhoods of the complete-graph feature map
Learner observes per-criterion losses; movement cost lambda*||s_t - s_{t-1}||_1 in regret
The learner knows the signal strength gamma and the eigenvalue growth constant kappa (used to set the warm-up length)
settings.definition_quote: In many applications, the true dependency graph G may be unknown. ... Assumption B: Minimum Signal Strength ... Assumption C: Diverse Contexts.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial full-information OCO with movement costs and switching budget
unmapped: Movement cost lambda*||s_t - s_{t-1}||_1 in regret
Expected number of state updates limited by a switching budget M known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: In this setting, the loss functions \ell_t(s) are arbitrary convex functions chosen by an adversary. The objective is to minimize the regret with movement costs ... subject to the constraint that the expected number of updates is at most M.

conditions: movement cost bounded by lambda per switch
tuning: confidence radius beta_{t,i} from Lemma (confidence ellipsoid) with confidence delta

source.label: th:regret-lazy-graph-LinUCB
source.quote: Assume the movement cost is bounded by $\lambda$ per switch. Let $d_i$ be the dimension of the feature map for criterion $i$, and $d_{\max} = \max_i d_i$. The cumulative regret of \textsc{LazyGraphLinUCB} is bounded by: \Reg_T \le \wt O( \sqrt{T} \sum_{i=1}^k d_i + \lambda k^2 d_{\max} \log T ).

results.notes: Theorem does not state probability; proof conditions on good event of probability >= 1-delta. LCB argmin may be non-convex so compute not stated.

symbols.dp_i: feature dimension of criterion i under proxy super-graph G'

conditions: learner uses a proxy graph G' that is a super-graph of the true graph (E subset of E')

source.label: cor:misspecification
source.quote: Suppose the learner operates using a proxy graph $\cG'$ such that $E \subseteq E'$ (a super-graph). Let $d'_i$ denote the feature dimension induced by $\cG'$. Then, \textsc{LazyGraphLinUCB} remains valid and guarantees a regret bound scaling with the proxy dimensions: \Reg_T \le \wt O( \sqrt{T} \sum_{i=1}^k d'_i + \lambda k^2 d'_{\max} \log T ).

results.notes: Learner knows a super-graph rather than exact graph.

conditions: there exists a graph (k disjoint cliques) and loss functions achieving the bound

source.label: th:lower-bound
source.quote: For any learning algorithm, there exists a graph structure $\cG$ and a sequence of loss functions such that the expected regret is lower bounded by: \E[\Reg_T] = \Omega( \sqrt{T} \sum_{i=1}^k d_i ).

results.notes: Proof reduces to k independent d_i-dimensional linear bandits using Dani et al. 2008 lower bound.

symbols.Delta_deg: maximum neighborhood size max_i |N(i)| of dependency graph

conditions: Assumption A: the LCB objective satisfies the PL condition so block coordinate descent reaches the global minimizer
tuning: lambda_reg chosen sufficiently large to satisfy Assumption A

source.label: th:async_regret
source.quote: Let $\Delta = \max_i |\cN(i)|$ be the maximum degree of the dependency graph. In the regularity regime where $\lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}$ is chosen sufficiently large to satisfy Assumption~A (see Lemma~\ref{lemma:assumption-a-justified}), the cumulative regret of the asynchronous algorithm is bounded by: \Reg_T \le \wt O( \sqrt{T} \sum_{i=1}^k d_i + \lambda \Delta d_{\max} k \log T ).

results.notes: Paper's Delta is the max degree, renamed Delta_deg. Probability type not stated in theorem.

symbols.d_i: true feature dimension of criterion i
symbols.d_total: feature dimension of the complete (dense) graph
symbols.kappa: linear growth rate of minimum eigenvalue of covariance (Assumption C)

conditions: Assumption B: minimum signal strength |theta*_{i,j}| >= gamma for true neighbors
Assumption C: lambda_min(V_{tau,i}) >= kappa*tau during warm-up

source.label: th:adaptive_regret
source.quote: Set the warm-up length to: $\tau = \frac{16 \beta_{T}^2}{\kappa \gamma^2}$ ... Under Assumptions B and C, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the algorithm recovers the true graph $\h \cG = \cG$, and the total regret is bounded by: \Reg_T \le \wt O( \frac{d_{\mathrm{total}}^{1.5}}{\kappa \gamma^2} + \sqrt{T} \sum_{i=1}^k d_i + d_{\mathrm{total}}^2 \log T ).

results.notes: Movement term written without lambda in the theorem; recorded as stated.

bound.expression_latex: \wt O( d_{\mathrm{eff}} \sqrt{k T} + \lambda k^2 d_{\max} \log T )

conditions: Assumption D: global loss decomposes over maximal cliques with unique clique parameters w*_C
d_eff = sum over maximal cliques of d_C

source.label: th:joint_regret
source.quote: Let $d_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sum_{C \in \cC} d_C$ be the sum of the dimensions of the maximal cliques. The cumulative regret of the Joint-LazyGraphLinUCB is bounded by: \Reg_T \le \wt O( d_{\mathrm{eff}} \sqrt{k T} + \lambda k^2 d_{\max} \log T ).

results.notes: d_eff here is the sum of clique dimensions, not the kernel effective dimension; reused canonical name loosely. Probability not stated in the theorem.

symbols.M: switching budget (expected number of state updates)

conditions: domain diameter D bounds both l1 and l2 diameters

source.label: th:lazy_ogd
source.quote: Let the loss functions $\ell_t$ be convex, $G$-Lipschitz, and defined over a domain of diameter $D$ (where $D$ bounds both the $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ diameters). For any switching budget $M \in [1, T]$, running Algorithm \ref{alg:lazy_ogd} with switching probability $p = M/T$ and learning rate $\eta = \frac{D}{G T}\sqrt{\frac{M}{2}}$ guarantees: \E[\Reg_T] \le \lambda D M + O( DG \frac{T}{\sqrt{M}} ).

results.notes: Leading term lambda*D*M is exact, second is O(); recorded jointly with O notation. D->diam_K, G->L_lip. Oblivious/adaptive adversary not specified.

conditions: loss decomposes additively into k independent components ell_t(s)=sum_i ell_{t,i}(s_i)

source.quote: Let the loss $\ell_t$ decompose into $k$ components with diameters $D_i$ and Lipschitz constants $G_i$. Given a vector of budgets $\bM$, the expected regret is bounded by: \E[\Reg_T] \le \sum_{i=1}^k ( \lambda D_i M_i + O( D_i G_i \frac{T}{\sqrt{M_i}} ) ).

results.notes: No proof given; follows from applying Theorem (th:lazy_ogd) per component.
